raw_response:
I am 78 years old now, and my legs are not as strong as they used to be, but I have farmed these fields in Quzhou for over sixty years. I know this land like the back of my hand. The North China Plain gives us two good harvests a year if you do not get lazy or greedy. I will stick to the winter wheat and summer maize rotation on my four mu of land because that is what the soil and the weather here are made for. I do not have the strength to try new crops like vegetables or fruit trees—they need too much bending and carrying, and the market prices go up and down too fast for an old man like me. I will buy improved wheat seeds and hybrid maize seeds from the village supply cooperative, the same kinds my neighbors use. I will rotary till before sowing the wheat, but for the maize I will sow directly after the wheat harvest without much tillage, because at my age I cannot turn the soil too many times. I will put down compound fertilizer as a base and top-dress with urea when the wheat turns green and when the maize is knee-high. I will irrigate the wheat three times and the maize twice if the sky does not give us enough rain. I will spray herbicide and pesticide twice for each crop—once for weeds and once for insects or disease—because losing even one tenth of the harvest hurts when you live on a pension and farming income. I expect about 560 jin per mu for the wheat and 680 jin per mu for the maize, which is enough to feed myself, sell a little, and pay for my grandson’s school supplies.
